title: Should Britain Abolish Jury Trials? (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，大家好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。在这档节目里，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事，一边了解这个世界稀奇古怪、妙趣横生的知识，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the law, specifically, jury trials in Britain, and their future.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊的是法律，具体来说，是英国的陪审团审判制度，以及它的未来。

sentences.en: The role of jury trials is a subject of ongoing debate, and the law might well be changing, so today we're going to look at the unusual idea and the uneven history of the jury, and at how twelve strangers with no legal training can decide whether someone is guilty or not guilty.
sentences.zh: 陪审团审判所扮演的角色一直是争论不休的话题，相关法律也很可能即将发生变化，所以今天我们要来看看陪审团这个不同寻常的构想，以及它跌宕起伏的历史，还有十二个没有受过法律训练的陌生人，是如何决定一个人是否有罪的。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话不多说，直接开始吧。

sentences.en: Imagine you are charged with a crime in England today.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，今天你在英格兰被指控犯了罪。

sentences.en: Not a minor traffic offence. Something serious.
sentences.zh: 不是什么轻微的交通违规，而是相当严重的罪行。

sentences.en: Fraud, perhaps, or assault. You maintain that you are innocent.
sentences.zh: 也许是诈骗，或者是人身伤害。你坚称自己是清白的。

sentences.en: You are certain you can prove it. And of course, you are innocent.
sentences.zh: 你很确定自己能证明这一点。而且，你当然是无辜的。

sentences.en: You listen to this show, which means you are an upstanding, law-abiding member of society.
sentences.zh: 你会听这档节目，这就说明你是一个正派守法的社会一员。

sentences.en: But somehow, somewhere, you've been accused and charged with a crime.
sentences.zh: 但不知怎的，在某个地方，你还是被指控并被起诉犯了罪。

sentences.en: Your lawyer tells you to expect your case to come to court in approximately three years.
sentences.zh: 你的律师告诉你，你的案子大概要等上三年左右才能开庭。

sentences.en: Possibly four. Some cases, he tells you, are now being scheduled to start in 2029.
sentences.zh: 也可能是四年。他告诉你，有些案子现在被排到了2029年才开庭。

sentences.en: Until then, you'll just need to sit tight.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，你只能干等着。

sentences.en: The possible verdict will be hanging over you.
sentences.zh: 那个尚未到来的判决，会一直悬在你头顶。

sentences.en: It will be the first thing you think about when you wake up, and the last thought you have before you go to sleep every night.
sentences.zh: 它会是你每天早上醒来第一个想到的事，也会是你每晚入睡前最后一个念头。

sentences.en: This is the reality of the Crown Court system in England and Wales in 2026.
sentences.zh: 这就是2026年英格兰和威尔士刑事法院系统的现实状况。

sentences.en: There are more than 78,000 cases waiting to be heard.
sentences.zh: 目前有超过78,000起案件在排队等待审理。

sentences.en: The backlog — the number of cases sitting in this queue — has roughly doubled since before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 积压案件的数量——也就是排在这条队伍里的案件数——比疫情之前大约翻了一番。

sentences.en: And it is still growing. And let's say you are the victim of a crime.
sentences.zh: 而且这个数字还在持续增长。再假设一下，你是某起犯罪的受害者。

sentences.en: It's the same wait, just from the other side.
sentences.zh: 等待的时间是一样的，只不过是从另一个角度去承受。

sentences.en: You might have to wait two, three, even four years until you can have some kind of closure.
sentences.zh: 你可能得等上两年、三年，甚至四年，才能获得某种意义上的了结。

sentences.en: And all that time, the person accused may still be walking free.
sentences.zh: 而在这整段时间里，被指控的那个人可能依然自由地走在街上。

sentences.en: Some victims, perfectly understandably, wait so long for their day in court that they simply give up and drop the charges.
sentences.zh: 有些受害者——这完全可以理解——等待开庭的时间实在太长，干脆就放弃了，撤销了指控。

sentences.en: The government's response, which was announced earlier this year by the Justice Secretary David Lammy, is radical.
sentences.zh: 政府给出的应对方案十分激进，这项方案是今年早些时候由司法大臣戴维·拉米(David Lammy)宣布的。

sentences.en: The basic idea is to reduce the number of cases going to a jury trial, and to reserve jury trials more clearly for the most serious offences.
sentences.zh: 其基本思路是减少交由陪审团审判的案件数量，把陪审团审判更明确地留给最严重的罪行。

sentences.en: The Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is working its way through Parliament as this episode is being recorded, would remove the rights of defendants to elect a jury trial for what are called “either-way offences” — things like fraud, robbery, and certain drug offences.
sentences.zh: 《法院与裁判庭法案》(Courts and Tribunals Bill)目前正在议会审议过程中——就在这期节目录制的同时——该法案将取消被告在所谓"可选审判方式罪行"上选择陪审团审判的权利，这类罪行包括诈骗、抢劫，以及某些毒品犯罪。

sentences.en: These are offences that are serious enough to go to the Crown Court but not the most serious crimes.
sentences.zh: 这些罪行严重到足以提交刑事法院审理，但还算不上最严重的罪行。

sentences.en: At the moment, a defendant charged with an either-way offence can choose whether to be tried by magistrates — who sit without a jury — or by a jury in the Crown Court.
sentences.zh: 目前，被指控犯有"可选审判方式罪行"的被告，可以选择由治安法官(没有陪审团)审理，还是交由刑事法院的陪审团审理。

sentences.en: That choice, the government says, must go.
sentences.zh: 政府表示，这种选择权必须取消。

sentences.en: And it's worth being clear about what this proposal does not include.
sentences.zh: 值得说清楚的是，这项提案并不涉及哪些内容。

sentences.en: Murder. Rape. Terrorism. Grievous bodily harm.
sentences.zh: 谋杀、强奸、恐怖主义、严重人身伤害。

sentences.en: Nobody in government is suggesting that the most serious crimes should be tried without a jury.
sentences.zh: 政府内部没有任何人主张，最严重的罪行应该不经陪审团审判。

sentences.en: The proposal is specifically about this middle tier of offences, for now at least.
sentences.zh: 这项提案针对的，至少目前来说，是这类处于中间层级的罪行。

sentences.en: Now, the legal community in Britain is, to put it mildly, alarmed.
sentences.zh: 而英国法律界的反应，说得委婉一点，是相当警觉。

sentences.en: Lawyers, barristers, and legal academics have all come out strongly against the bill, with many arguing that the right to a jury trial is a fundamental safeguard against the overreach of the state.
sentences.zh: 律师、出庭律师和法律学者纷纷强烈反对这项法案，许多人认为，陪审团审判的权利是防止国家权力过度扩张的一项根本性保障。

sentences.en: It exists for a reason, they say, and is one of the foundations of a just and fair society.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这项权利的存在是有原因的，它是一个公正、公平社会的基石之一。

sentences.en: So, is it really? Where does the idea of jury service come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，事实真是如此吗？陪审团服务这个概念究竟从何而来？

sentences.en: How is it used, and what are some of the most famous cases of juries in action?
sentences.zh: 它是如何运作的？又有哪些陪审团断案最著名的案例？

sentences.en: Well, let’s start with what a jury trial actually is, because it might be quite an unfamiliar concept, especially if you come from a country with a civil-law system.
sentences.zh: 好，我们先来说说陪审团审判到底是什么，因为对一些人来说，这可能是个相当陌生的概念，尤其是如果你来自一个大陆法系国家。

sentences.en: In England, when you are charged with a serious criminal offence, your guilt or innocence is decided not by a judge, but by a jury.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰，当你被指控犯有严重刑事罪行时，决定你有罪还是无罪的，不是法官，而是陪审团。

sentences.en: A jury is a group of twelve ordinary citizens, chosen at random, who are called to sit in court and listen to the evidence presented by both sides.
sentences.zh: 陪审团由十二名随机挑选出来的普通公民组成，他们被召集到法庭上，聆听控辩双方提出的证据。

sentences.en: At the end of the trial, they retire — they leave the courtroom and deliberate together in private — and they return with a verdict.
sentences.zh: 审判结束后，他们会退庭——离开法庭，私下一起商议——然后带着裁决结果回到法庭。

sentences.en: Guilty, or not guilty. The judge's job is to oversee the proceedings, to advise the jury on points of law, and if the verdict comes back guilty, they will decide on the appropriate punishment, based on the severity of the crime.
sentences.zh: 有罪，或者无罪。法官的职责是主持整个庭审程序，就法律要点向陪审团提供指导，如果最终裁决为有罪，法官则会根据罪行的严重程度决定相应的量刑。

sentences.en: But the central factual question — did this person commit this crime? — this is answered by the twelve random strangers pulled in off the street.
sentences.zh: 但那个核心的事实问题——这个人到底有没有犯下这桩罪行？——则要由这十二个从街头随机拉来的陌生人来回答。

sentences.en: Or rather, not literally pulled in off the street, but chosen at random from the electoral roll.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，倒也不是真的从街头拉来的，而是从选民名册中随机挑选出来的。

sentences.en: This is what lawyers call the adversarial system.
sentences.zh: 这就是法律人士所说的"对抗制"。

sentences.en: Two sides — the prosecution and the defence — present their cases to a neutral decision-maker.
sentences.zh: 控辩双方——控方和辩方——各自向一个中立的裁决者陈述己方的主张。

sentences.en: It's quite different from the more inquisitorial system used in France, Germany, and most of continental Europe, where the judge takes a far more active role in investigating the facts, and where ordinary citizens play a much smaller part.
sentences.zh: 这与法国、德国以及欧洲大陆大多数国家所采用的更偏"纠问制"的制度截然不同，在那种制度下，法官在调查事实方面扮演着远为主动的角色，而普通公民所起的作用则要小得多。

sentences.en: And this jury system, and the principle behind it, goes back a very long way.
sentences.zh: 而陪审团制度以及其背后的原则，历史可以追溯得相当久远。

sentences.en: The first jury-like systems we know of appeared in ancient Athens, around the sixth century BC.
sentences.zh: 我们已知最早的类似陪审团的制度，出现在古代雅典，大约是在公元前六世纪。

sentences.en: Athenian citizens could be called to serve as dikastai — citizen judges — who would hear arguments and decide cases by majority vote.
sentences.zh: 雅典公民可能被召集去担任"dikastai"(公民审判员)，他们负责聆听双方的论证，并通过多数票来裁决案件。

sentences.en: Sometimes there were hundreds of them sitting on a single trial.
sentences.zh: 有时候，一场审判会有多达数百人参与其中。

sentences.en: The most famous example is the trial of Socrates in 399 BC, in which five hundred citizens voted to condemn him to death.
sentences.zh: 最著名的例子，就是公元前399年对苏格拉底(Socrates)的审判，当时有五百名公民投票判处他死刑。

sentences.en: It was, in some ways, the first great jury trial.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是历史上第一场伟大的陪审团审判。

sentences.en: And it produced one of history's most controversial verdicts.
sentences.zh: 而它也产生了历史上最具争议的裁决之一。

sentences.en: The English jury, however, developed much later.
sentences.zh: 不过，英国的陪审团制度是后来才逐渐发展起来的。

sentences.en: In etymological terms, as the keen linguists among you might have guessed, the English word "jury" comes from the Old French "juré," meaning "sworn" — those who have taken an oath, who have made a promise.
sentences.zh: 从词源上讲，可能已经有语言学爱好者猜到了，英语单词"jury"来自古法语的"juré"，意思是"宣过誓的"——指那些已经宣誓、做出承诺的人。

sentences.en: What the English did was formalise it. In 1166, King Henry II issued what is called the Assize of Clarendon.
sentences.zh: 英国人所做的，是把这套做法正式确立下来。1166年，亨利二世(Henry II)国王颁布了所谓的《克拉伦登法令》(Assize of Clarendon)。

sentences.en: It required that in each district, twelve local men of good standing should be assembled to report on crimes and settle disputes.
sentences.zh: 该法令要求，在每个辖区，都要召集十二名当地有声望的男子，负责举报罪行、裁决纠纷。

sentences.en: This was not yet the modern jury as we know it today, but it established the principle: twelve local people, deciding together.
sentences.zh: 这还不是我们今天所熟知的现代陪审团，但它确立了一项原则：由十二名当地人共同做出决定。

sentences.en: Then, in 1215, came Magna Carta — the great document forced on King John by his barons.
sentences.zh: 然后，到了1215年，《大宪章》(Magna Carta)问世——这是由男爵们强迫约翰(King John)国王签署的一份伟大文件。

sentences.en: It contains a clause that has shaped the law ever since: "No free man shall be seized, imprisoned, or dispossessed, except by the lawful judgement of his equals."
sentences.zh: 其中有一条条款，自此深刻塑造了后世的法律："任何自由人，非经其同侪的合法审判，不得被拘捕、监禁或剥夺财产。"

sentences.en: The important idea there is not the exact modern mechanism, but the principle behind it: that justice should not simply be the arbitrary will of the ruler.
sentences.zh: 这里重要的并不是那套具体的现代机制，而是它背后的原则：正义不应该仅仅是统治者的一意孤行。

sentences.en: The lawful judgement of "his equals" — people like him.
sentences.zh: "同侪"的合法审判——也就是与他地位相当的人。

sentences.en: Peers judging peers. So when the British government talks about removing jury trials for a large category of offences, it's not proposing a minor administrative tweak.
sentences.zh: 由同等身份的人来审判同等身份的人。所以，当英国政府谈到要为一大类罪行取消陪审团审判时，这可不是在提议某种无关紧要的行政微调。

sentences.en: It's proposing to dismantle a mechanism of justice that has existed, in some form, for over eight hundred years.
sentences.zh: 它是在提议拆除一套以某种形式存在了八百多年的司法机制。

sentences.en: Now, if you live in a country where the legal system doesn't use juries, you might be thinking: why would you need them?
sentences.zh: 如果你生活在一个法律体系不使用陪审团的国家，你可能会想：为什么会需要陪审团呢？

sentences.en: It's a perfectly reasonable question to ask: why use ordinary people at all?
sentences.zh: 这是个完全合理的问题：为什么一开始就要让普通人参与其中？

sentences.en: Why not have a judge decide every case? After all, they are a professional, trained in the law, experienced in weighing evidence.
sentences.zh: 为什么不干脆让法官来裁决每一个案子？毕竟他们是专业人士，受过法律训练，也有权衡证据的丰富经验。

sentences.en: The answer is about power. A judge is appointed by the state.
sentences.zh: 答案关乎权力。法官是由国家任命的。

sentences.en: They work within the system. They have a career to protect and professional instincts shaped by years inside the legal establishment.
sentences.zh: 他们在这个体制内工作，有自己的职业生涯需要维护，也有经年累月在法律体系内培养出的职业本能。

sentences.en: A jury is none of those things. It is twelve people chosen at random, with no career to protect, no deference to authority, and no obligation to the government.
sentences.zh: 陪审团则完全不同。它是十二个随机选出的人，没有职业生涯需要顾及，不会对权威唯命是从，也不对政府负有任何义务。

sentences.en: That randomness is the point. You cannot bribe, pressurise or intimidate twelve strangers before they walk into the room, because you do not know who they are.
sentences.zh: 这种随机性正是关键所在。你无法在十二个陌生人走进法庭之前贿赂、施压或恐吓他们，因为你根本不知道他们是谁。

sentences.en: A single judge, however, is a known quantity.
sentences.zh: 而单独一名法官，却是一个已知的对象。

sentences.en: If a government wants to convict someone, a judge is a far easier target than a jury.
sentences.zh: 如果政府想给某人定罪，针对一名法官要比针对一个陪审团容易得多。

sentences.en: There is also something important about legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有关于正当性的重要一面。

sentences.en: When a jury convicts someone, the wider community can see that the verdict came from ordinary people — people like them.
sentences.zh: 当陪审团判定某人有罪时，更广泛的社会大众能够看到，这个裁决是出自普通人之手——和他们一样的人。

sentences.en: It was not handed down by a distant official.
sentences.zh: 而不是由一个高高在上、遥不可及的官员做出的判定。

sentences.en: Yes, it can be slow and frustrating, but for the most part, it works.
sentences.zh: 没错，这个过程可能又慢又让人沮丧，但在大多数情况下，它是行之有效的。

sentences.en: Twelve people need to be sufficiently convinced, based on the evidence they have seen, that someone is either guilty or not guilty.
sentences.zh: 十二个人需要根据他们所看到的证据，被充分说服，认定某人有罪或无罪。

sentences.en: Sometimes, however, a jury does something unexpected.
sentences.zh: 然而，有时候陪审团也会做出出人意料的事。

sentences.en: It acquits someone who is, by any technical reading of the law, guilty.
sentences.zh: 他们会判某个从法律技术层面来看明明有罪的人无罪。

sentences.en: Lawyers call this jury nullification. It is the power of a jury to refuse to convict even when the facts seem clear, because the jurors believe that convicting would produce an unjust result.
sentences.zh: 法律界把这种情况称为"陪审团废止权"(jury nullification)。这是陪审团即便在事实看似清楚的情况下，依然拒绝定罪的权力，因为陪审员们认为，定罪会造成不公正的结果。

sentences.en: The law says he did it; we say it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 法律说他确实做了；而我们说，这并不重要。

sentences.en: We'll come to a few examples of this in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会讲到几个这方面的例子。

sentences.en: Now, the most famous jury trial in living memory is probably the OJ Simpson case, in 1995.
sentences.zh: 在当代人的记忆中，最著名的陪审团审判，大概要数1995年的辛普森(OJ Simpson)案。

sentences.en: You might know this story already, and if you're a member, you might remember it from episode number 409.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经听过这个故事了，如果你是我们的会员，或许还记得我们在第409期节目里讲过它。

sentences.en: But as a quick reminder, the former American football star was acquitted of murdering his ex-wife, who was found not guilty, despite overwhelming physical evidence against him.
sentences.zh: 但简单提醒一下：这位曾经的美式橄榄球明星，被指控谋杀他的前妻，尽管对他不利的物证堆积如山，他最终还是被判无罪。

sentences.en: Now, rather than revisit that case, let me tell you about a few lesser-known cases — because they show something more specific about how the system actually works.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们这次不打算重温那个案子，而是想跟你们讲几个不那么为人所知的案例——因为它们更具体地展示了这套制度到底是如何运作的。

sentences.en: The first dates from 1670, when the principle of jury nullification was established in England.
sentences.zh: 第一个案例要追溯到1670年，那一年，"陪审团废止权"这项原则在英格兰被正式确立。

sentences.en: This is the case of William Penn, the man who would later found the colony of Pennsylvania in America.
sentences.zh: 这就是威廉·佩恩(William Penn)的案子，他后来在美洲建立了宾夕法尼亚殖民地。

sentences.en: Now, Penn was a Quaker preacher. He was accused of holding what was called an unlawful religious assembly — in other words, preaching publicly in a way that the authorities said was illegal.
sentences.zh: 佩恩是一名贵格会传教士。他被指控举行所谓的"非法宗教集会"——换句话说，以一种当局认定为非法的方式公开传教。

sentences.en: Penn was clearly guilty under the law. But the jury refused to convict him.
sentences.zh: 按照法律，佩恩显然是有罪的。但陪审团拒绝判他有罪。

sentences.en: The judge was furious. He locked the jurors up without food or drink to force a guilty verdict.
sentences.zh: 法官勃然大怒，把陪审员们关起来，不给食物也不给水，想逼他们做出有罪的裁决。

sentences.en: They still refused. A higher court eventually ruled that a jury could not be punished for its verdict, whatever that verdict might be.
sentences.zh: 陪审员们依然拒绝屈服。最终，上级法院裁定，陪审团不能因其裁决——无论裁决结果是什么——而受到惩罚。

sentences.en: And that principle has remained ever since.
sentences.zh: 这项原则从那以后就一直延续了下来。

sentences.en: Now, fast-forward three centuries. It is February 1985, and a man named Clive Ponting is sitting in the dock at the Old Bailey — London's most famous criminal court.
sentences.zh: 现在，时间快进三个世纪。1985年2月，一个名叫克莱夫·庞廷(Clive Ponting)的人坐在老贝利(Old Bailey)——伦敦最著名的刑事法院——的被告席上。

sentences.en: Ponting is a senior civil servant at the Ministry of Defence.
sentences.zh: 庞廷是英国国防部的一名高级公务员。

sentences.en: He has leaked classified documents to a Labour Member of Parliament — documents that revealed the Argentine Navy ship General Belgrano had been sailing away from the British exclusion zone when it was sunk during the Falklands War, killing 323 Argentine sailors.
sentences.zh: 他向一位工党下议院议员泄露了机密文件——这些文件揭示出，阿根廷海军的"贝尔格拉诺将军号"(General Belgrano)在福克兰战争中被击沉时，其实正驶离英国划定的禁区，这次击沉事件造成323名阿根廷海员丧生。

sentences.en: Importantly, the Conservative government had told Parliament something quite different.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，保守党政府此前向议会所说的情况，与此大相径庭。

sentences.en: Ponting is charged under the Official Secrets Act.
sentences.zh: 庞廷被依据《官方保密法》(Official Secrets Act)提起公诉。

sentences.en: He is, on the face of it, obviously guilty.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，他显然是有罪的。

sentences.en: He admits leaking the documents. The judge, summing up, tells the jury that "the interests of the state" are the same as the interests of the government, and directs them accordingly.
sentences.zh: 他承认泄露了文件。法官在总结陈词时告诉陪审团，"国家利益"等同于政府利益，并据此对陪审团做出相应指示。

sentences.en: The jury retires. It comes back with a verdict of not guilty.
sentences.zh: 陪审团退庭商议，回来后给出的裁决是无罪。

sentences.en: The government is furious. But the jury had evidently decided that telling Parliament the truth about the deaths of 323 people was not a crime worth punishing.
sentences.zh: 政府勃然大怒。但陪审团显然认定，把323人死亡的真相告诉议会，并不是一桩值得被惩罚的罪行。

sentences.en: And this theme has continued to the modern day.
sentences.zh: 而这个主题一直延续到了今天。

sentences.en: In January 2022, four defendants appear before a jury at Bristol Crown Court, charged with criminal damage.
sentences.zh: 2022年1月，四名被告出现在布里斯托尔刑事法院的陪审团面前，被控刑事毁坏罪。

sentences.en: They had pulled down the statue of Edward Colston, an eighteenth-century slave trader, during the Black Lives Matter protests of June 2020, and they had thrown the statue into Bristol harbour.
sentences.zh: 在2020年6月"黑人的命也是命"(Black Lives Matter)抗议活动期间，他们推倒了十八世纪奴隶贩子爱德华·科尔斯顿(Edward Colston)的雕像，并把雕像扔进了布里斯托尔港。

sentences.en: They do not deny doing it. The footage exists.
sentences.zh: 他们并不否认自己做过这件事。相关录像也确实存在。

sentences.en: The jury finds them not guilty, by eleven votes to one.
sentences.zh: 陪审团以十一票对一票的结果，判他们无罪。

sentences.en: The then Justice Secretary was furious. And so were many members of the public.
sentences.zh: 当时的司法大臣勃然大怒，许多公众成员也同样如此。

sentences.en: Others pointed out that the jury had done exactly what juries are meant to do: reach a verdict the jurors considered just, based on the full circumstances of the case.
sentences.zh: 但也有人指出，陪审团做的正是陪审团本该做的事：基于案件的完整情况，做出他们认为公正的裁决。

sentences.en: Critics, however, argued that this looked uncomfortably close to jurors overriding the law because they sympathised with the defendants.
sentences.zh: 然而，批评者则认为，这看起来太像是陪审员因为同情被告，而凌驾于法律之上，让人感到不安。

sentences.en: This sparked a fierce debate over the role of juries: should juries be allowed, in effect, to rewrite the law through their verdicts, or is that unpredictability precisely part of their constitutional function?
sentences.zh: 这引发了一场围绕陪审团角色的激烈争论：陪审团是否应该被允许，实质上通过自己的裁决来改写法律？还是说，这种不可预测性恰恰正是他们宪制职能的一部分？

sentences.en: Now, you may have strong views on this, but what is clear is that these cases make an argument for juries that no efficiency review ever will.
sentences.zh: 你可能对此有自己强烈的看法，但可以肯定的是，这些案例为陪审团制度提供了一种论据，而这种论据是任何效率评估都无法给出的。

sentences.en: The government couldn't predict how any of those juries would vote.
sentences.zh: 政府根本无法预测这些陪审团中的任何一个会如何投票。

sentences.en: That uncertainty — that independence from the state — that is exactly what the bill would start to erode.
sentences.zh: 而这种不确定性——这种独立于国家之外的特质——正是这项法案将要开始侵蚀的东西。

sentences.en: No longer would twelve strangers be responsible for deciding whether someone is guilty.
sentences.zh: 将不再由十二个陌生人来负责决定一个人是否有罪。

sentences.en: That responsibility would instead fall to magistrates or a judge.
sentences.zh: 这份责任将转而落到治安法官或法官身上。

sentences.en: Now, the government is not necessarily saying that this is a better system in terms of fairness; its argument is primarily practical.
sentences.zh: 政府并没有说这在公平性上是一套更好的制度；它的理由主要是出于现实考量。

sentences.en: The backlog is over 78,000 cases and growing, with official modelling suggesting it could rise to 200,000 by 2035.
sentences.zh: 积压案件已经超过78,000起，而且还在增长，官方的模型预测，到2035年这个数字可能会攀升到20万起。

sentences.en: Victims are waiting years. Fewer jury trials, so the argument goes, will be faster and cheaper, and will allow the most serious cases to receive jury trials without the same years-long wait.
sentences.zh: 受害者要等上好几年。按照这种论调，减少陪审团审判的案件数量，能让审判更快、成本更低，也能让最严重的案件不必再经历同样长达数年的等待，就能获得陪审团审判。

sentences.en: But the counterargument is powerful. The value of the jury lies precisely in its awkwardness — the fact that it's slow, unpredictable, and answerable to no one.
sentences.zh: 但反对的论点同样有力。陪审团制度的价值，恰恰就在于它的"麻烦"——它慢、不可预测、也不向任何人负责这一点。

sentences.en: A state that can imprison its citizens without needing to persuade ordinary members of the public is a state with considerably more concentrated power.
sentences.zh: 一个无需说服普通公众就能监禁公民的国家，是一个权力高度集中得多的国家。

sentences.en: And then there is the slippery slope argument.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有所谓"滑坡"式的论点。

sentences.en: The current proposal is careful to exclude the most serious crimes.
sentences.zh: 目前的提案很谨慎地把最严重的罪行排除在外。

sentences.en: But the critics' concern is not really about where the line is drawn today.
sentences.zh: 但批评者真正担心的，其实并不是今天这条界线划在哪里。

sentences.en: It's about what happens once you accept that the line can be moved at all.
sentences.zh: 而是一旦你接受了这条界线本身是可以被移动的，接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Once you establish that efficiency can override eight hundred years of constitutional principle, the question is: how far?
sentences.zh: 一旦确立了"效率可以凌驾于八百年宪制原则之上"这个先例，问题就变成了：这条路会走多远？

sentences.en: A government that reduces jury rights for fraud and robbery has already won the argument in principle.
sentences.zh: 一个已经削减了诈骗和抢劫案陪审团权利的政府，实际上已经在原则层面赢得了这场争论。

sentences.en: What stops a future government from extending that logic to other offences, if a new backlog develops, or a new pressure emerges?
sentences.zh: 如果日后又出现新的积压，或者面临新的压力，又有什么能阻止未来的政府把这套逻辑延伸到其他罪行上呢？

sentences.en: A poll in 2025 found that fifty-four per cent of people in Britain would prefer to be tried by a jury if accused of a crime.
sentences.zh: 2025年的一项民调发现，如果被指控犯罪,54%的英国民众更愿意接受陪审团的审判。

sentences.en: Even knowing all the delays and imperfections, a majority of the population trusts twelve strangers more than it trusts a single judge.
sentences.zh: 即便明知这套制度存在种种延误和缺陷，大多数民众依然更信任十二个陌生人，而不是一名法官。

sentences.en: And that, perhaps, is the most important thing to understand about jury service.
sentences.zh: 而这一点，或许正是理解陪审团制度最重要的地方。

sentences.en: It is not simply a mechanism for producing verdicts.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是一套用来产出裁决结果的机制。

sentences.en: It is an expression of a belief — the belief that ordinary citizens, and not the state, should have the final say over whether one of their number is imprisoned.
sentences.zh: 它是一种信念的体现——一种认为应该由普通公民、而不是国家，来最终决定他们当中的一员是否该被监禁的信念。

sentences.en: Britain is debating whether to give that up, and, in so doing, is asking whether eight centuries of constitutional principle are really worth sacrificing for the sake of clearing an administrative backlog.
sentences.zh: 英国正在争论是否要放弃这一点，而在这场争论中，它其实也是在追问：为了清理行政积压，牺牲掉八个世纪的宪制原则，真的值得吗？

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on jury trials.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天这期关于陪审团审判的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目足够有趣，也希望你从中学到了一些新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: Do juries exist in your country? If so, how do they work?
sentences.zh: 你的国家有陪审团制度吗？如果有，它是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: And are there similar proposals to change them?
sentences.zh: 有没有类似的提案想要对它做出改变？

sentences.en: Let me know in the comments below, if you're listening to this somewhere where you can comment, and for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 如果你是在一个可以留言的平台上收听这期节目，欢迎在下方评论区告诉我；而对于我们的会员来说，你们可以直接前往我们的社区论坛——网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com——和其他"好奇的头脑"们畅聊起来。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 以上就是 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家平安，我们下期节目再见。
